question:
In a Young’s Double Slit Experiment (YDSE), the slit separation is $d$ and the screen is placed at a finite distance $D$ from the slit plane (so you cannot assume $D\gg d$). Let $P$ be a point on the screen at a vertical displacement $y$ from the central point $O$.

A student uses the approximation $\Delta \approx \dfrac{dy}{D}$ to locate fringes even when $D$ is not much larger than $d$.

Evaluate the validity of this approximation by doing the following:

(i) write the exact path difference $\Delta=S_1P-S_2P$ in terms of $D$, $d$, and $y$, and

(ii) explain under what condition(s) this exact expression reduces to the approximate form $\Delta\approx \dfrac{dy}{D}$.

Conclude whether the student’s use of the approximation is justified in the finite-distance setup.

options.A: The approximation is always valid because the path difference in YDSE is exactly $\Delta=\dfrac{dy}{D}$ for any $D$.
options.B: The approximation is invalid in general. The exact path difference is $\Delta=\sqrt{D^2+\left(y+\dfrac{d}{2}\right)^2}-\sqrt{D^2+\left(y-\dfrac{d}{2}\right)^2}$, and it reduces to $\Delta\approx\dfrac{dy}{D}$ only when $D\gg d$ and $|y|\ll D$ (small-angle region).
options.C: The approximation is valid whenever $d\gg D$ because then the rays are nearly parallel and $\Delta\approx\dfrac{dy}{D}$.
options.D: The approximation fails because the exact path difference depends only on angle and is $\Delta=d\sin\theta$ for all screen positions.
